claim.markdown_says: ## 8.4.3.3.4 General rules   (ISO_COBOL.md line 7001)   -- while its three peers are '#### 8.4.3.3.1 General' (6956), '#### 8.4.3.3.2 General format' (6961) and '#### 8.4.3.3.3 Syntax rules' (6966)
claim.why_it_matters: The general rules of reference-modification -- the clause that defines leftmost-position, length and EC-BOUND-REF-MOD -- sit at H2 while their three sibling subclauses sit at H4, so the general rules detach from 8.4.3.3 Reference-modification and read as a top-level section.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Nothing is missing and no meaning changes; the claim is a pure markdown-formatting observation, mis-filed as 'missing-heading'. (1) The heading is PRESENT and CORRECT. Rendered p162 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v162/spec_p162.png) prints the bold heading '8.4.3.3.4 General rules' immediately below the NOTE that closes the p161 syntax rules. ISO_COBOL.md line 7001 carries exactly that clause number and exactly that title, in exactly that position, preceded at line 7000 by the correct machine-readable anchor ''. The full hierarchy is encoded in the dotted number '8.4.3.3.4' and in the anchor, both transcribed verbatim, so any citation lookup or outline built on clause numbers resolves correctly. Nothing was dropped, reworded, renumbered or relocated. (2) The PDF supplies NO heading-level cue to lose. Comparing the rendered pages side by side, '8.4.3.3.4 General rules' on p162 is typographically IDENTICAL to '8.4.3.3.1 General', '8.4.3.3.2 General format' and '8.4.3.3.3 Syntax rules' on p161 (E:/Temp/specrecon/v161/spec_p161.png) -- same bold face, same point size, same left margin -- and identical to the PARENT heading '8.4.3.3 Reference-modification' as well. ISO uses uniform heading typography at these depths; depth is carried solely by the clause number. There is therefore no PDF property that '## vs ####' can be said to contradict. This is a transcription markup choice, not a fidelity defect. (3) The '## vs ####' split is not an anomaly -- it is the file-wide norm, and '##' is the MAJORITY form. Heading depth in ISO_COBOL.md is noise everywhere: 280 four-or-more-level clause headings are '##' against only 24 that are '####'. Within clause 8.4.3 alone the same four-part subclause set appears at H2 (8.4.3.1.1/.2/.3, 8.4.3.2.4), at H3 (all of 8.4.3.4.* through 8.4.3.8.*, 8.4.3.10.*), and mixed within one subclause (8.4.3.9.1/.2 are '####' while 8.4.3.9.3/.4 are '##'; 8.4.3.11.1 is '###' while 8.4.3.11.2/.3/.4 are '##'). Three-level clauses are equally erratic ('## 8.1.3 COBOL character repertoire' vs '### 8.1.1 General'; '## 8.4.3 Identifiers' vs '### 8.4.2 Uniqueness of reference'). Line 7001 is the same pattern as its own cousin 8.4.3.2.4, flagging one instance of a document-wide convention would require flagging several hundred. (4) The stated rationale is factually wrong. '##' cannot 'read as a top-level section' in this file: H2 is the level used for the 1261 '## Page NNN' page markers, and H1 is used for running headers. H2 carries no top-level-clause semantics here. (5) The cause is page-break furniture, an explicitly excluded category. The mis-level occurs on the first heading after a page boundary, alongside the same boundary rendering the running header as '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' (H1) on p162 where p161 renders it as bold text '**ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)**'. Both are the OCR heading-detector resetting at the page break. (6) The normative content of p162 was read in full against the page image and matches verbatim: general rules 1) through 5), sub-items a), b) and c), the closing EC-BOUND-REF-MOD / REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH paragraph, and the final NOTE on UTF-16 surrogate pairs citing 8.5.1.4. No text discrepancy exists on this page.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a discrepancy. The heading '8.4.3.3.4 General rules' is present in ISO_COBOL.md (line 7001) with the correct clause number, correct title, correct position and a correct '' anchor, and the PDF prints it in typography indistinguishable from its three siblings and from its own parent -- so no level information exists in the source to be lost. The only observation that survives is a cosmetic markdown artifact with zero semantic consequence: heading DEPTH is unreliable throughout the entire transcription (280 deep-clause headings at '##' vs 24 at '####'; within 8.4.3 the same subclause pattern appears at H2, H3 and mixed), and line 7001 follows the file's majority '##' form while its p161 siblings happen to use the minority '####' form. If heading depth is ever to be normalized, it must be done as a single document-wide pass driven by the dotted clause number -- not logged as a per-page content discrepancy.
